lines.text: You're blind for about forty minutes every day. And you've never noticed.
Your eyes don't glide across things. They jump, three or four times a second.
Mid-jump, everything would smear like a shaky phone video.
So your brain just cuts the feed.
Then it fills the gap with whatever you saw next, and lies about the timing.
That's why the first tick of a clock sometimes lasts too long.
Want proof? Find a mirror. Look at your left eye, then your right.
You'll never see your own eyes move.
Your friend standing behind you sees them move just fine.
Add up all those tiny blackouts, and you're blind for about forty minutes every day.
